name: Arrival
text: Where the track comes in: the row of cabins set into the old quarry wall, their living roofs level with the forest above.

name: Lagoon shore
text: The natural lagoon, cleaned by plants instead of chlorine. Every cabin faces it through a front of glass, floor to ceiling.

name: Cabin deck
text: The deck of cabin 4. The roof reaches 1.5 m past the glass with no posts: the summer sun never touches it and nothing blocks the view.

name: Inside the cabin
text: Inside cabin 4: one bedroom and a kitchen island behind the glass. 45 cm walls of local rammed earth soak up the afternoon heat and give it back at night.

name: On the living roof
text: On the living roof of cabin 2: native grasses on 20 cm of soil. It insulates and slows the rain, and from the hill the cabin disappears.

name: The homesite
text: A homesite of about a hectare on the private side: the protected forest behind, the valley in front. Two earth volumes stepped with the slope.

name: The terrace
text: The terrace and the 12 m pool, heated by the sun and filtered without chlorine, looking east over the valley.

name: The living room
text: The living room: rammed-earth walls and a glass front to the valley. Three bedrooms, about 180 m² in all; the bedroom wing sits back for privacy.

name: On the living roof
text: On the living roof: native grasses on 20 cm of soil, the terrace and the pool below, the valley beyond. From the trail above you see grass, not a house.

name: The mango tree
text: The old mango tree and its two granite boulders, where the trail across the hill ends.

name: The homestead
text: Already built: the brick house with its clay tile roof, the solar array beside it, and the forest of Cerro Kavaju behind.

name: By the pond
text: The pond, dug into the slope: the wooden cabin at the edge of the forest above it, the bell tent and the quincho, among pindó palms.
